what: CAE builds flight simulators and runs pilot training centres. Airlines send their pilots to CAE to be certified, and air forces use its simulators for military training.
customers: Airlines, business jet operators, air forces and healthcare training institutions.
money: flight simulators and commercial pilot training
moat: Simulators certified for a specific aircraft type, placed in training centres near airline hubs, where the capital cost and certification make a new entrant impractical.
risks: 46 times earnings after years of write-downs on defence contracts bid too cheaply
Only three analysts cover the stock
opportunities: $523M of free cash flow, far above reported earnings, at about 17 times cash flow
Revenue grew from $2.7B to $3.4B in four years
A global pilot shortage means airlines must train more pilots, which is exactly what CAE sells
watch: Civil training centre utilisation and whether defence margins recover.
